questions.q: Q17. The dog ____ is chasing the squirrels belongs to Brijesh. [CDS II 2022]
questions.s: "That" is used for animals like "dog". जानवरों (dog) के लिए 'that' का प्रयोग सही है।

questions.q: Who was / there but she to look / after the family in distress?
o: Who was
there but she to look
after the family in distress?
No error
questions.s: Explanation:-  Yahan 'but' ka matlab 'ke sivay ya ke alawa' hai. Yaani but yahan par preposition ki tarah work kar rha hai. Isliye uske baad Objective case ka use hoga. 'she' nahi 'her' ka use kiya jayega.

questions.q: If your coming home tomorrow (a) / let me know at what time (b) / I can expect you. (c) / No error (d)
o: let me know at what time
questions.s:
The word your shows possession, but here we need the verb you are to express an action. So, your coming is wrong; it should be you are coming.
Correct sentence: If you are coming home tomorrow, let me know at what time I can expect you.

questions.q: The articles/ published in this magazine/ are better than/ that magazine.
questions.s: Explanation:- Ek magazine ke Articles ka Comparison dusre magazine ke Articles se hi hoga isliye yahan those ka prayog hoga sath hi Published Adjective jo first clause me de rakha hai. Use bhi hume meaning ko same rakhne ke liye, repeat karna padega. Isliye 'those published in that magazine' ka use hoga.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select "no substitution required".

He stood up from their chair to signal the end of the meeting.
o: up from his
upon of his
No improvement
below in their
questions.s:
up from his

We generally use the pronoun 'their' for a plural subject and 'his/her' for a singular subject. Similarly, in the given sentence, the subject (He) is singular. Hence, 'up from his' is the most appropriate answer.

questions.q: She asked for your opinion and valued it more than her.
o: She asked for your
it more than her
questions.s:
The sentence has an error. The correct form should be: (c) it more than hers. A possessive pronoun can be used as the object of a verb.

So, the corrected sentence is: “She asked for your opinion and valued it more than hers.”

questions.q: Their favor is always appreciated by us.
questions.s:
"Favour from them" - This phrase uses the possessive adjective "their" to indicate that the favor belongs to "them." It specifies whose favor is being discussed, emphasizing that it is the favor from them that is significant.

So, the corrected sentence is: “Favor from them is always appreciated by us.”

questions.q: Can anybody tell me? (a) / why Randhir absented (b) / from the meeting. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: "Absent" as verb needs reflexive pronoun. Change "Randhir absented" to "Randhir absented himself" - reflexive pronoun required with this verb.
